transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-02-10 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Thompson, Ethan Park (Redwood); Priya Nair, Marcus Doyle, Sofia Rios (Cedarlane)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on tenant segmentation, KMS/residency requirements, GDPR constraints for EU customers, and acceptable logging footprint. Customer leaning toward a Private deployment or Dedicated with strong tenant isolation. Discussed tradeoffs and next steps to scope a short POC.

Topics covered:
- Tenant isolation patterns (single-tenant v. multi-tenant, logical isolation)
- Key management: KMS vs HSM, key residency, key-escrow policies
- GDPR data residency and data subject request paths
- Log retention, redaction and audit evidence for regulators
- Hosted fallback patterns and canary routing for resilience

Action items captured in call notes (also listed in metadata).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me is Ethan our SE.
[00:06] Priya: hi, thanks, appreciate you carving time, got a few folks here.
[00:10] Marcus: hey. quick note from me: compliance is the gating item so we want to focus on keys and logs.
[00:16] Ethan: totally, we can start with an architecture sketch and then dig into KMS and logging options.
[00:22] Sofia: sounds good. we run model inference for KYC workflows, so PII and EU customer data flows in.
[00:28] Maya: perfect, that's helpful. are you currently using cloud KMS today or an on-prem HSM?
[00:34] Priya: we have a mix — AWS KMS for general services, but high-risk flows have keys in a vendor HSM in our data centers.
[00:40] Marcus: and regulators want to see key custody and residency controls — specifically some of our EU entity data must remain in EU zones, right.
[00:46] Ethan: understood — Redwood supports a couple of patterns: 1) Private deployment into your VPC where keys never leave your control, 2) Dedicated with customer-managed KMS where key material is held by you and Redwood services call into your KMS over a private link, 3) hosted with envelope encryption and redaction.
[01:10] Priya: can you explain the difference practically? like, what changes for our operations if we pick Dedicated vs Private?
[01:16] Maya: sure — Dedicated is a Redwood-managed cluster reserved for your account in our cloud region; you'll get tenant isolation at the infra level and we can integrate with your KMS via private connectivity. Private is our full private control plane option — the control plane is in your VPC or on-prem, you get more control over audit trails and where logs are stored.
[01:36] Marcus: and for auditors, do we get logs that prove key access and request tracebacks?
[01:40] Ethan: yes, both options provide audit logs. For Private, logs can be stored in your S3/ELK stack and we can turn off certain telemetry. For Dedicated we provide tenant-level audit packages and you can request extended retention, though we do have some limitations on host-level metrics retention unless you opt into the premium observability add-on.
[02:06] Sofia: about logs — we need to be able to redact customer identifiers from payloads before anything leaves the VPC. is that supported?
[02:12] Maya: we have a configurable pre-send redaction hook and also prefix/KV cache options so you can strip PII. In Private, that hook runs inside your network. In Dedicated we can run the hook in-host but data may cross our network links — would need an agreement.
[02:32] Marcus: ok, GDPR items — data subject requests, right to erasure; how does Redwood handle model inputs that include personal data?
[02:38] Ethan: two parts — first, retention: you control how long we keep request logs and you can request immediate purge for PII. Second, for model outputs, we recommend an application-layer approach: app persists identifiers in customer-owned stores, and inference payloads reference opaque IDs. For PII accidentally sent, we can configure redaction and set zero retention on the hosted side or configure Private so nothing leaves your network.
[03:06] Priya: timeline — we have a regulatory review planned in six weeks. we need a POC that shows residency and key custody controls by then.
[03:14] Maya: that sounds doable. typical POC is two weeks for setup + two weeks for benchmarks and evidence collection. we'll prepare a runbook.
[03:22] Sofia: for benchmarking we need latency numbers for our 512-token average sequences and throughput for batch inference. can Redwood run that inside our VPC?
[03:30] Ethan: yes, if we do Private or Dedicated with direct connectivity we can run the same runtime and return token-level latency traces. we'll also include per-token cost estimates.
[03:40] Marcus: one more — key escrow. our compliance team sometimes requires key escrow to a local custodian for emergency access. does Redwood support escrow or split-keys?
[03:47] Ethan: we can work with split-key models or customer-controlled escrow, depends on your KMS/HSM. For Private, you control both the keys and any escrow policy. For Dedicated we can integrate with your HSM provider for split-key flows.
[04:03] Priya: good. another item: cross-border backups. backups of inference logs must not replicate to non-EU regions for EU customers. can you restrict backups?
[04:12] Maya: yes — region locking on storage is supported in Private; for Dedicated we can configure geo-restrictions per customer but we need to add a policy to prevent cross-region replication. we'll confirm details in the runbook.
[04:26] Sofia: any regulatory evidence pack you provide — e.g., for GDPR and FINRA — what does that include?
[04:31] Ethan: typically SOC 2 Type II reports, a data flow diagram we map to your tenancy, KMS access logs, and sampling of audit trails showing key usage and request IDs. For FINRA-like needs we'll add message trails and retention proofs. Some items require on-prem log collection.
[04:51] Marcus: do you do redaction at token-level or only payload-level? we have examples where PII is embedded mid-sentence.
[04:57] Ethan: we offer both heuristics and deterministic hooks. The deterministic hook is best — run a tokenizer-based sanitizer inside your environment before hitting the runtime. We also have in-flight redaction that can mask tokens but that leaves some metadata. We'll share the redaction doc.
[05:16] Maya: real quick — has anyone here run a Redwood POC before?
[05:20] Priya: no, first time.
[05:22] Sofia: we've done other LLM vendors internal POCs but not Redwood.
[05:26] Maya: ok, baseline then — we'll propose a small Private or Dedicated POC with three test cases: 1) EU-residency-only pipeline, 2) key-custody test with HSM integration, 3) log-redaction stress tests.
[05:40] Priya: that aligns with our compliance asks. can you do HSM integration with our Thales box?
[05:46] Ethan: yes — we've done Thales and Gemalto in past deployments. we'll need admin-level access or a service account to test the key wrapping flows.
[05:56] Marcus: about network connectivity — do you support AWS PrivateLink or direct connect for Dedicated?
[06:02] Ethan: Dedicated supports PrivateLink and we can set up IP allowlists. Private supports Direct Connect/VPN since the control plane sits in your VPC.
[06:12] Sofia: what about SSO and RBAC mapping? our security team uses SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[06:18] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync; we can map roles into fine-grained RBAC and lock admin actions behind MFA + IP ranges.
[06:28] Priya: fine. pricing — high level ballpark for Dedicated or Private?
[06:33] Maya: we'll send a pricing matrix but ballpark: Dedicated reserved capacity starts with a monthly commitment for N GPUs; Private has a licensing fee plus ops support, tends to be higher but gives you full control. We'll include tiers and the add-on for extended audit retention.
[06:47] Marcus: competitors — are there differences vs AWS Bedrock when it comes to keys and residency?
[06:52] Ethan: Bedrock can live in your account but some orchestration features and model optimizations differ. Also our focus is on predictable inference economics and production tooling like KV caching and rollout controls; key residency patterns are similar but our Private option gives more turnkey control for audits.
[07:12] Sofia: I'd like to call out a technical constraint: our inference payloads sometimes exceed 1MB because of large document contexts. any input size limits?
[07:20] Ethan: typical runtime limits 1–2MB for request size depending on the model variant and sequence handling. For large contexts we recommend chunking and referencing with persistent embeddings. We'll document limits and guidance.
[07:34] Priya: okay let's talk about acceptance criteria for the POC — what do you need from us and what will you deliver?
[07:38] Maya: we'll need three things from you: 1) sample payloads and expected outputs, 2) KMS/HSM endpoint details and a test key that can be used for wrapping tests, 3) a list of regulators / specific evidence items you need. We'll deliver a runbook, a deployed instance (Private or Dedicated), bench results (latency, throughput), audit traces showing key usage, and a redaction verification report.
[08:04] Marcus: sounds good. any blockers you foresee?
[08:07] Ethan: potential delay is establishing network connectivity and getting HSM credentials — those often require approvals. Other than that, we should be clear.
[08:16] Priya: timeline check — we'll aim to get approvals for connectivity in a week. if so, can you start provisioning the environment the following week?
[08:23] Maya: yes, once we have approvals and the signed POC SOW we can schedule provisioning.
[08:28] Sofia: question about data minimization — we want to avoid sending entire customer history to the model. do you have suggestions for in-line filters?
[08:34] Ethan: yes, Redwood Optimize includes guidance for prompt engineering and batching to minimize tokens. We also advise client-side scrubbing and only sending necessary context. We can include suggested scrubbing regexes in the runbook.
[08:48] Priya: auditability — if a data subject asks for a copy of the data used, do we get an export of all requests for a given user id?
[08:55] Ethan: you can export request logs tied to an opaque request id. If you want user-level exports, we recommend tying requests to your user ids server-side and storing the minimal mapping in your system so you can satisfy DSARs. We'll show an example mapping in the POC.
[09:10] Marcus: any encryption-in-transit specifics? TLS ver 1.3? mutual TLS?
[09:14] Ethan: we support TLS 1.2+ and 1.3, and for Private/Dedicated we can enable mutual TLS and client certs.
[09:22] Maya: quick check — any other stakeholders we should loop in? legal or privacy folks?
[09:27] Priya: yes, I'll loop in Legal and our Privacy officer, Elena, on the follow-ups.
[09:31] Maya: great. we'll send the SOC2/HIPAA materials and the runbook.
[09:35] Sofia: one operational note — we want to see keys rotated without downtime. is rotation automation supported?
[09:41] Ethan: yes, key rotation with zero-downtime wrapping is supported for our runtime when using enveloped keys. For HSM we can do a key swap process — we'll include steps.
[09:53] Marcus: is there any telemetry we cannot disable? we have to prove no telemetry leaves for some EU regulated flows.
[09:59] Ethan: certain platform health metrics are collected by default but in Private we can disable telemetry collection and only route logs to your collectors. In Dedicated we can minimize telemetry and set a retention policy but some host-level metrics are necessary unless you take Private.
[10:16] Priya: okay, let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:19] Maya: recap: Maya to send SOC2 + HIPAA one-pager and pricing matrix by Friday (2027-02-12). Ethan to prepare POC runbook and benchmark template by 2027-02-15. Sofia to share sample payloads and retention policy by 2027-02-14. Maya to propose POC schedule for week of 2027-02-22.
[10:40] Priya: sounds good. Marcus: we'll also confirm network approvals this week.
[10:45] Maya: great. any final Qs?
[10:47] Sofia: just one — for the POC will there be a dedicated SE assigned?
[10:50] Ethan: yes I'll be the primary SE and we'll bring in one of our infra SREs for the provisioning window.
[10:56] Priya: thanks everyone.
[10:58] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up over email with the materials. meeting ends.
